gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own 350W Solar Panel has a 33 V open-circuit voltage, so two of them wired in series give 66 V, which is above the Elite 200 V2's 12–60 V solar input. BLUETTI still sells the 'Elite 200 V2 + 2×350W Solar' bundle ($2,148), and its in-the-box list has no parallel (Y) connector. For a solar-recharged fridge backup, that pair has to be wired in parallel, or the shopper should use the 2×200W bundle instead.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. basc.pnnl.gov (PNNL/DOE) covers surge (up to 3× running watts), EnergyGuide kWh/365 and the fact that 1–2 kWh with PV runs a fridge for many hours. It gives no input voltage window and names no panel or station. itechguides.com lists 10 ms UPS claims and FridgePower + BlueCell 200 expansion to 8,064 Wh, so that part of the angle is already covered. It also says to 'verify the accessory and input voltage against the exact model' but gives no voltage window for any model and never names a panel-to-station mismatch. Neither page gives the Elite 200 V2's 12–60 V/20 A/1,000 W PV limit or a panel Voc. I did not open ranks 2–3 and 5–17 (solargenadvisor, powerstations.reviews, stormwatts and others), so one of them could state a voltage window. The finding only decides the solar part of the set, not whether the fridge runs, so I scored it 2, not 3.
kit_items: power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh LFP, 2,600 W continuous). It is already in Dealectric's catalog and ChatGPT also showed it as a card. Its PV input is 12–60 V / 20 A / 1,000 W max on BLUETTI's US page.

solar panels: BLUETTI 200W Portable Solar Panel ×2 (SP200L), sold in BLUETTI's own 'Elite 200 V2 + 2×200W Solar' bundle. The 200 W panels are recommended over the 2×350W bundle because two 350 W panels (33 V Voc each) exceed the 60 V input in series. Whether two SP200L panels in series stay under 60 V is unconfirmed: I could not open a BLUETTI page for the SP200L Voc (see unsourced).

alternative station if the shopper wants a fridge-specific UPS unit: BLUETTI FridgePower (2,016 Wh, 1,800 W / 3,600 W surge, <10 ms UPS, expands with BlueCell 200 to 8,064 Wh). The base $949 listing and the $999 'FridgePower + Display 1' listing differ by $50, which suggests the base unit ships without the detachable Display 1. BLUETTI's page does not say that outright.

findings.label: solar (PV) input window
findings.note: From the page FAQ: 'PV input: Elite 200 V2: 12V-60V/20A, 1,000W max'. I saw the same text on the elite-200-v2-2-pv350d page.

findings.label: open-circuit voltage (Voc)
findings.note: The page says 'a 33V open-circuit voltage (Voc)'. It ships with a 20A MC4-to-XT60 cable (1.5 m), lists the Elite 200 V2 and Elite 100 V2 as compatible, and gives no series/parallel guidance.

findings.label: series-wiring conflict
findings.value: 2 × 33 V = 66 V Voc in series, which is 6 V over the 60 V max input
findings.note: Arithmetic uses the two BLUETTI pages above. Voc rises further in cold weather. The bundle's 'IN THE BOX' lists only the AC charging cable, documentation, Elite 200 V2 and grounding screw, with no Y/parallel connector. Bundle price $2,148.00.

findings.label: AC output / AC input
findings.value: 2,600 W continuous (Power Lifting up to 3,900 W on pure resistive loads only); AC input 1,800 W max
findings.note: The 3,900 W Power Lifting figure is for resistive loads, so it does not cover a fridge compressor start. No surge rating is given.

findings.label: capacity, output, UPS, expansion
findings.value: 2,016 Wh LFP; 1,800 W continuous / 3,600 W surge; <10 ms UPS switching; expandable to 8,064 Wh; 4 W idle draw
findings.note: Expansion bundles use BC200 (BlueCell 200). The UPS bypass/pass-through max power is not stated on the page.
